ul.li: Single-core turbo refers to the processor's ability to temporarily boost the frequency of a single active core beyond its base operating level, enabling peak performance for lightly threaded or latency-sensitive workloads.
This feature is particularly relevant in scenarios where applications rely on fast execution of single-threaded tasks.

Achieving the maximum turbo frequency depends on favorable thermal and power conditions, making it essential for system designers to understand how to optimize their platforms to unlock this performance potential.
